types.name: DeferredDeleteQueue
types.doc:
GPU resources submitted here are held for N frames, so nothing is freed while
an in-flight command buffer may still read it. Flush once per frame from the
main loop with the current frame index.

members.name: Submit
members.signature: void Submit(std::function<void()> destructor, const void* owner = FModuleAnchor::Here())
members.doc:
The destructor lambda runs m_frameDelay frames later. `owner` names
the submitting module (FModuleAnchor): a module that unloads with
releases still queued has them run while its code is still mapped,
since both the lambda and the std::function managing it are that
module's code and nothing could call either afterwards.

members.name: RunAllInModule
members.doc:
Runs and drops every queued release a module submitted — the unload
sweep. Returns how many ran.

members.name: Flush
members.doc: Runs every destructor whose deadline has passed.

members.name: FlushAll
members.doc: Immediate — only safe when the GPU is known idle, e.g. at shutdown.

members.name: IsIdle
members.doc:
True when nothing enqueued is still pending or running: the caller (the
only thread that enqueues) is then the only one that can record until it
enqueues again. Always true while the thread is disabled.

members.name: Init
members.doc:
Runs on the runnable's thread before Run(). Returning false aborts: the
thread exits and Exit() does NOT run.

members.name: Run
members.doc:
The thread body; the return value is the OS thread's exit code, 0 for
success. Long-running loops must poll a stop flag the implementation owns.

members.name: Stop
members.doc: Called from another thread. Override to set the flag Run() polls.

members.name: Exit
members.doc:
Runs on the runnable's thread after Run() returns, always, unless Init()
returned false.

members.name: Create
members.signature: static FRunnableThread* Create(FRunnable* runnable, std::string name, EThreadPriority priority = EThreadPriority::Normal)
members.doc: Takes ownership of `runnable` and deletes it after Exit() returns.

members.name: Stop
members.doc:
Polite shutdown: call runnable->Stop() then join. Idempotent.
Returns whatever Run() returned (or 0 if it hadn't started).

members.name: WaitForCompletion
members.doc:
Joins without calling Stop() first — only safe when the runnable is known
to be self-terminating. Idempotent.

members.name: ~FRunnableThread
members.doc: Destructor calls Stop() if still running.

types.name: FGraphEvent
types.doc:
Handle to a scheduled task. The graph owns one ref per pending subsequent,
plus one per outstanding caller handle.

members.name: Wait
members.doc:
Blocks until the task and every transitive prerequisite completes. NOT
re-entrant: calling Wait() from inside a task on the same graph deadlocks.

members.name: WaitFor
members.doc: Waits at most `milliseconds`; true once the task has completed.

members.name: ParallelFor
members.doc:
Runs [0, count) in chunks across pool workers and blocks until every
iteration has run. Ordered or thread-pinned work wants AddTask instead.

members.name: SpinUpDedicatedThread
members.doc:
Idempotent. Auto-fires on the first AddTask targeting the slot, but call
it during engine init so thread priority and name are set from frame
zero. Once spun up, AddTask(thread) queues instead of running inline.

members.name: Shutdown
members.doc:
Flushes queued tasks — they all run on their own threads first — then
joins every dedicated thread. Idempotent; called from Engine::Shutdown
via FCoreDelegates::OnPreEngineShutdown.

members.signature: static void WaitLogged(EPhaseThread self, const char* what, const std::function<bool(uint32_t sliceMs)>& waitSlice)

types.name: JobCounter
types.doc:
Tracks job completion: a job submitted against a counter won't run until it
reaches 0. The counter also carries a priority floor — the most aggressive
priority any dependent has asked for. SubmitWithDependency raises it and the
JobSystem promotes in-flight jobs signalling the counter to match, so a High
dependent never stalls behind Low signal jobs.

members.name: SetException
members.doc:
The first exception a job under this counter threw. The job still counts
as done — a throw that skipped the decrement hung every waiter forever —
and JobSystem::WaitForCounter rethrows it on the waiting thread, the way
std::future does, so a fatal error still reaches that thread's handler.

members.name: WaitFor
members.doc:
False on timeout with the counter still outstanding. WaitForCounter uses
it to turn a silent forever-block into a diagnosable stall.

members.name: BoostPriorityTo
members.doc:
Priority inheritance. Lower numeric value = higher priority (High=0,
Normal=1, Low=2), so boosting is an atomic min. Returns true only when
the floor actually moved — callers use that to decide whether to scan
the queues and promote jobs.

types.name: FInlineJob
types.doc:
Type-erased callable with a fixed inline buffer. Every engine call site fits
inline — the largest is FTaskGraph's wrapped task at ~112 bytes. Callables
that exceed the buffer, need stronger alignment, or have a throwing move
constructor fall back to one heap allocation.

members.name: ParallelFor
members.signature: JobCounterPtr ParallelFor(uint32_t count, uint32_t batchSize, const std::function<void(uint32_t begin, uint32_t end)>& func, JobPriority priority = JobPriority::Normal)
members.doc: Splits [0, count) into batches and returns a counter to wait on.

members.name: ParallelFor
members.signature: JobCounterPtr ParallelFor(uint32_t count, const std::function<void(uint32_t begin, uint32_t end)>& func, JobPriority priority = JobPriority::Normal)
members.doc:
Picks batchSize so each worker gets ~4 batches, trading granularity
against per-batch overhead. Use the explicit overload to control it.

members.name: WaitForCounter
members.doc:
Runs the counter's own still-queued jobs on the calling thread while it
waits, and sleeps only when the rest are already running on workers. A
waiter used to sleep through the whole batch — the game thread idled
for every parallel section, a 1/(workers+1) share of it lost on a
four-core handheld — and a worker waiting on its own pool could only
hope another worker got there.

members.name: IsWorkerThread
members.doc:
True when the calling thread is one of this pool's workers. Callers that
want to apply backpressure (block until the pool drains) MUST check this
first: a worker blocking on the pool's own progress deadlocks it.

types.doc:
Auto-reset event. Windows backs it with a native Event, which beats a
condition variable for plain signal/wait; elsewhere it is a mutex plus
condition variable. The handle is owned by the platform layer.
